Chief Executive’s Monthly Management Report – 28th February 2026
 
 
A Chara,  
I enclose the above report for your statutory consideration, this report has also been prepared under Section 136 
& 138 of the Local Government Act, 2001. The attached report is the Chief Executive’s Monthly Management 
Report for February 2026, detailing activities, updates, and progress across various departments of Louth County 
Council. 
Below is a summary of key achievements and actions under various directorates from the Chief Executive Report 
for February 2026: 
 
1. Finance and System Support 
• 
Total expenditure to 27th February was €27,157,177 (13% of the annual budget).  
• 
Total income was €52,320,260 (26% of the annual budget). 
• 
Total debtor balance as of 27th February 2026, was €65,847,333, with government debtors accounting 
for €13,320,173. 
• 
 696 IT support calls were logged, with 91.67% resolved. The email filtering system identified 14% of 
inbound emails as potentially harmful.  
• 
Louth County Council website received 15,947 unique page views in February. 
2. 
Economic Delivery 
• 
Festival Grant Initiative allocated and letter of offer for €200,000 to support over 90 events and 
festivals. 
• 
Development of Brigid’s Way cross-county route and reimagined Boyne Valley Drive projects are 
underway. 
• 
Collaboration with five county councils and Fáilte Ireland to develop the Táin Trail. 
• 
Local Enterprise Week launched with workshops, training, and events to support businesses all well 
attended and received. 
• 
Rates Waiver Scheme introduced to incentivize new businesses in vacant commercial premises. 
• 
23 business advice clinics and 4 training courses held in February. 
• 
There were 53 planning applications received during the month of January which 49 were valid, in 
addition there  were 25 responses received during the month to requests for further information and 23 
Pre-Planning Requests received. 
• 
In January 24 Planning Enforcement Complaints Investigated. 
• 
Work continues with two workshop son the 2027 Pre-Draft County Development Plan.  
 
3. Operations & Environment Delivery 
• 
Storm Chandra occurred in February which involved a very successful response by the Operations team, 
responding with sandbags, water pumps, and drainage works across affected areas. Pothole repairs, street 
cleaning, and coastal protection works continue to be carried our post the storm as a priority. 
• 
Extensive road and pothole repairs were completed in Dundalk, Drogheda, and Ardee. 
• 
 Waste enforcement investigated 14 complaints, issued 21 fixed penalty notices for littering, and conducted 
water and air pollution inspections. 
• 
 51 applications were received under the Community Climate Action Programme, totalling €2,360,344.37. 
Funding applications were submitted for 7 biodiversity projects. 
• 
To the end of 25th Feb, ERCC had processed 191 calls for Louth Fire,18% on the same period last year 
(234 calls for service).  
• 
There were 23 additional calls for Louth Fire in Co. Meath, 5% on the same period in 2025 (22 calls). 
4. Corporate Services 
• 
In February 2026 Customer Services dealt with 19,314 queries inclusive of 10,163 calls, 1,264 e-mails and 
7,887 counter queries. 11,215 (58%) of queries received were dealt with at first point of contact. 
• 
Age-Friendly Initiatives, Expansion of the Garden Care & Repair project to Dunleer and hosting of a Road 
& Community Safety Event in Drogheda. 
• 
Public Participation Network (PPN), Secretariat meeting held to allocate funding and finalize training 
programs for 2026. 
• 
Healthy Louth, Supported the launch of the Primary Health Care for Travellers Project.

6. Major Capital Projects & Infrastructure Delivery 
• 
Urban and Rural Regeneration Projects:  
o 
Progress on St. Nicholas Quarter and Backlands Regeneration, Longwalk Urban Framework 
Plan, and Dunleer Energising the Community projects. 
o 
Funding approved for Town and Village Renewal Scheme projects, including Carlingford, 
Clogherhead, Collon, Haggardstown, and Omeath. 
• 
Roads Projects:  
o 
Construction of Narrow Water Bridge continues. 
o 
Progress on N53 Hackballscross to Rassan, N52 Ardee Bypass, Boyne Enterprise Link Road, 
and Port Access Northern Cross Route. 
• 
Flood Defence and Coastal Erosion Projects:  
o 
Interim measures approved for Carlingford and Greenore Flood Relief Project. 
o 
Public participation days planned for Dundalk and Blackrock Flood Relief Projects. 
• 
Active Travel Projects: €4 million allocated for Active Travel and Safe Routes to Schools projects, with 
several projects in various phases of development. 
 
I would like to express my sincere appreciation for the exceptional commitment, and professionalism 
demonstrated by the entire Louth County Council team, across all directorates 
  
I encourage all members to read the full report, which reflects the breadth and impact of the remarkable work 
carried out across the organisation.

ArcGIS Online – Public Planning Register Map Viewer 
 
The LCC GIS Team recently updated the online Planning Register Map Viewers. These can be accessed from 
the Online Planning Application and Maps section user Services> Planning on the Louth County Council 
website.  
 
 
 
The data in the application is updated regularly to include all planning applications. There were 4,874 views of 
the application between 01/02/2026 and 27/02/2026, an average of 187 views a day in February. 
 
 
Cyber Security Training  
 
February’s cyber security training emphasised the importance of protecting organisational data when working 
remotely by minimising stored data, avoiding public Wi-Fi, staying aware of surroundings, and promptly 
reporting any suspected incidents to prevent breaches. It also highlighted how attackers increasingly exploit 
unsecured or spoofed Wi-Fi networks including sophisticated drone-based hotspots reinforcing the need for 
staff to treat all networks with caution and connect only through trusted, verified sources.

Táin Trail 
The Táin Trail retraces the journey taken by Queen 
Medb (Maeve) of Connacht and her armies during 
the Irish epic legend of Táin Bó Cuailgne.  It travels 
from Queen Medb’s palace in Rathcroghan, County 
Roscommon, across to the Cooley Peninsula in 
County Louth crossing through Counties Longford, 
Westmeath and Meath.  The five respective County 
Councils, with Fáilte Ireland, are collaborating to 
develop a project to sign post the route for local 
communities and tourists.

Rates Waiver Scheme 
The Council has introduced a Rates Waiver Scheme 
for 2026 with the aim to assist and provide incentives 
for new businesses to locate in vacant commercial 
premises in the town centres to encourage diversity 
of retail opportunities.  LEO Louth is promoting and 
supporting this scheme, which has been designed to 
reduce the financial pressure on new businesses 
setting up in premises that have been vacant for 
more than 12 months.  Eligible applicants can 
benefit from a phased waiver on commercial rates 
over a three-year period, offering significant savings 
during the critical early years of trading.  Businesses 
approved under the scheme will receive a full rates 
waiver in year one, followed by a 50 per cent 
reduction in year two and a 25 per cent reduction in 
year three.
